summary: The A5 e-hybrid quattro puts Audi's new-generation plug-in hardware — the same 270kW/500Nm and 25.9kWh gross (20.7kWh usable) pack as the Q5 e-hybrid — into a liftback body at $89,900, and for 2027 it is the A5 Audi is pushing: the 150kW petrol has been dropped and the 200kW TFSI quattro it matches on price is now customer-order only. Being lighter and lower than the Q5 buys it 97km of WLTP electric range against the SUV's 82km and 7.3L/100km with the battery flat, and at $89,900 it slips under the $91,661 fuel-efficient luxury car tax threshold; the family now also includes the $179,827 RS 5 Sedan, a 470kW V6 plug-in with a 22kWh usable pack and 78km of WLTP range that misses the 3.5L/100km test and pays full luxury car tax. Reviewers rate the pace, the range and the price parity, but are consistent about what the pack costs: 331 litres of boot against 445 in the petrol A5, a cabin of piano black with rattles reported on a launch car, and sport suspension on 20-inch wheels with no adaptive option.
pros: $89,900 is the identical list price to the 200kW TFSI quattro petrol A5 Sedan (now customer-order only) for 70kW more and a 5.1-second 0-100km/h, and the 2.6L/100km combined figure clears the 3.5L/100km fuel-efficient test — so the car is judged against the $91,661 LCT threshold rather than the $80,809 one and pays no luxury car tax at all, worth roughly $2,700

97km of WLTP electric range from a 20.7kWh usable (25.9kWh gross) battery — 15km more than the heavier Q5 e-hybrid's 82km on the same hardware, so a 30-45km Melbourne commute runs on electricity with margin either side

$8,300 cheaper than the $98,200 Mercedes-Benz C350e while making 270kW/500Nm to the Mercedes' 230kW/550Nm and matching the S5 for outputs; with the BMW 330e withdrawn from Australia the Mercedes is the only direct alternative, and it sits above the fuel-efficient LCT threshold where the Audi sits below

60g/km certified combined CO2 is half Victoria's 120g/km green passenger car threshold, so it pays $8.40 per $200 of duty instead of the $10.40 per $200 an $89,900 petrol A5 attracts — about $900 saved at the point of registration; the RS 5's 86-98g/km band also qualifies, which at $179,827 saves far more against the 18.00-per-$200 top tier
11kW three-phase AC charging fills the pack 0-100 per cent in about 2.5 hours, and the five-year unlimited-kilometre vehicle warranty is backed by eight years or 160,000km on the high-voltage battery
cons: The battery under the boot floor costs 114 litres: 331L seats-up and 1175L folded against 445L in the petrol A5 Sedan, a 26 per cent loss that is the single most-cited complaint in the Australian launch reviews and the reason the pack is worth checking against a pram or a set of golf clubs before signing; the RS 5 Sedan is no better at 331L/1170L

The 2.6L/100km label figure only holds if every trip starts charged — Audi's own WLTP figure with the battery discharged is up to 7.3L/100km for this 270kW, 20-inch specification and Chasing Cars measured 7.6L/100km in mixed driving, so a buyer who cannot charge at home is running a 2,095kg quattro on 95 RON; the 2,355kg RS 5 is rated at up to 10.0L/100km with the battery flat

Charging is AC-only at 11kW with no DC fast-charge hardware, so a flat battery on a road trip stays flat until you find a destination charger — and the 46-litre tank, down from 56 in the petrol car, gives back some of the touring range the plug-in gains

PHEVs lost the FBT exemption on 1 April 2025 and $89,900 is well clear of the $75,000 2027 FBT phase cap, so the novated-lease concessions that once carried the plug-in premium do not apply and the case rests on home charging; the RS 5's 4.2L/100km label fails the 3.5L/100km test, so it pays luxury car tax from the $80,809 threshold

The cabin draws consistent criticism: extensive gloss-black trim and hard plastics low down, ventilated seats a $2,200 option, and a CarsGuide launch car that had already developed rattles and creaks; the sport suspension on 20-inch wheels has no adaptive alternative and CarExpert called the steering numb
